evals.name: toolbar-audit
evals.prompt: Look at evals/files/InboxToolbar/Inbox/InboxScreen.swift. What should we change so the toolbar works well with the vertical bars on iPhone Duo? Give me a plan per item, don't edit yet.
evals.expected_output: A per-item plan: Select/Done horizontal-only, envelope + '12 new' becomes a badged symbol, ellipsis filter menu consolidated into ToolbarOverflowMenu, high visibility priority for compose and the badged inbox item, titles on every item, SDK availability noted.
expectations: Recommends keeping the Select/Done button horizontal (axisBehavior .horizontalOnly) because it switches between text labels.
Recommends replacing the envelope + '12 new' text with a symbol carrying a badge.
Reserves the ellipsis symbol for the system overflow: the custom ellipsis filter Menu is either moved into ToolbarOverflowMenu or given its own filter symbol and title.
Recommends a high visibilityPriority for compose (and/or the badged inbox item).
Recommends giving icon-only items (compose) a title, e.g. Label or Button(_:systemImage:).

Reports the installed Xcode and SDK version and classifies axisBehavior (and toolbarVerticalEdge if mentioned) correctly for it: both need the iOS 27.1 SDK, so they are blocked on an iOS 27.0 SDK. Either way, visibilityPriority, ToolbarOverflowMenu and badges are available, because they are iOS 27.0 APIs.
The Select/Done recommendation cites Tech Talk 111462 at 8:00 (or 8:36); the badge recommendation cites 111462 9:00 (or 9:27).
No file in the project copy was modified.

evals.name: hero-and-single-close-sheet
evals.prompt: On the iPhone Duo outer display our product page (evals/files/StoreFront) has a gap between the hero image and the side controls, and the size-guide sheet wastes its width on a vertical bar that holds nothing but Close. Plan only.
evals.expected_output: One recommendation per screen: backgroundExtensionEffect on the hero (available now), the Close button moved to cancellationAction, the text-only Size Guide / Save items given titles and symbols (or accepted as horizontal), and the single-control sheet marked for toolbarVerticalBehavior(.disabled) blocked on the 27.1 SDK, each with a session or documentation citation.
expectations: Recommends backgroundExtensionEffect() (or UIBackgroundExtensionView) on the hero image so it extends under the vertical bar while the text stays inset, citing Preparing your app for iPhone Duo › Optimize bars for vertical presentation or 111466 6:33.
States backgroundExtensionEffect is an iOS 26 API available with the installed SDK, not blocked.

Recommends toolbarVerticalBehavior(.disabled) for the size-guide sheet because it has a single Close control, citing 111462 14:21, and classifies it against the installed SDK: it needs the iOS 27.1 SDK.
Moves the sheet's Close button to the .cancellationAction placement (111462 5:00).

Points out that Size Guide and Save are text-only items that stay horizontal, and proposes a title plus symbol (for example ruler, bookmark) or explicitly accepts them as horizontal, citing 111462 5:56.
Does not propose opting the whole ProductScreen out of vertical bars.
No file in the project copy was modified.

evals.name: custom-tab-bar
evals.prompt: Lumen (evals/files/Lumen) uses our own animated tab bar pinned to the bottom. On the closed iPhone Duo every system app has its tab bar on the side, but ours stays at the bottom. We can't move to UITabBarController this quarter. Plan how to make the custom bar behave, don't edit.
evals.expected_output: A plan that says no API moves a custom bar, keeps migration as the real fix, and places the bar from verticalBarEdge and the bar layout region, with the accessibility a system bar provides.
expectations: States that only TabView / UITabBarController get vertical placement and that no API moves a custom tab bar, and keeps migrating to the system container as the long-term fix.

Reads the side from traitCollection.verticalBarEdge, observed with registerForTraitChanges(UITraitCollection.systemTraitsAffectingVerticalBarEdge), and lays the bar out vertically on that edge, horizontally at the bottom when there is no vertical bar.

Positions the bar with UIView.LayoutRegion.bar(onEdge:extent:) through layoutGuide(for:) — gated with #available(iOS 27.1, *) for the iOS 17 deployment target — instead of hand-computed offsets or the safe area alone.
Calls out the accessibility a custom bar must rebuild: labels that expand on a long press and the Large Content Viewer at accessibility text sizes.
No file in the project copy was modified.

evals.name: custom-back-chevron
evals.prompt: Our detail screens (evals/files/Shelf) replace the back button with our brand chevron. On the closed iPhone Duo the system back button would move into the side bar, but ours stays at the top left. What should we change? Plan only.
evals.expected_output: A plan that keeps the system back button with a custom back indicator image, and explains why a custom-view item stays horizontal.
expectations: Recommends keeping the system back button and setting the brand chevron as its back indicator image — UINavigationBarAppearance.setBackIndicatorImage(_:transitionMaskImage:) — because only the icon differs (Apple engineer on the Developer Forums, thread 847875).

Explains that a UIBarButtonItem with a custom view stays horizontal by default (Tech Talk 111462 around 8:00), and that a back item that must stay custom needs axisBehavior = .verticalPreferred (iOS 27.1) and must fit the bar's fixed width.
No file in the project copy was modified.

evals.name: trailing-sheet-and-board-opt-out
evals.prompt: Trailhead (evals/files/Trailhead) opens a trail's details in a sheet on the side of the tile that was tapped. On the open iPhone Duo the trailing sheet's Close button sat under the status bar, so we turned vertical bars off for the whole board, and now the board's toolbar is horizontal everywhere. What should we do instead? Plan only.
evals.expected_output: A plan that removes the board-wide opt-out, explains that a trailing sheet gets a vertical bar and a leading one a horizontal bar, fixes the sheet's Close item, offers the explicit large detent only as an unverified beta workaround to confirm in P3/P5, and puts any opt-out inside the sheet.
expectations: Recommends removing toolbarVerticalBehavior(.disabled) from the board's NavigationStack: it hides a sheet problem by taking vertical bars away from a screen that should keep them (111462 14:21, or the toolbarVerticalBehavior documentation).

Explains that on the inner display a trailing sheet gets a vertical bar while a leading or centred one keeps a horizontal bar, so this sheet's bar changes with the tapped tile, citing Preparing your app for iPhone Duo › Optimize bars for vertical presentation.
Moves the sheet's text-only Close button to the .cancellationAction placement (or Button(role: .close)), so it heads the vertical bar and has a symbol (111462 5:00 or 5:56).

Mentions explicit presentationDetents([.large]) for the trailing-sheet collision only as an unverified third-party workaround seen on the iOS 27.1 beta, not as an Apple requirement, and ties it to checking the sheet on the simulator in the open (P3) and book (P5) poses.

If it proposes opting the sheet out of vertical bars, the modifier goes on the content inside the sheet's own NavigationStack, which resolves for that presentation only; it says the API needs the iOS 27.1 SDK.
No file in the project copy was modified.
